title: Claims status regression
inputDescription: Repeatable workload fixtures/workload.json: 60 live-status requests from one customer (CUS-000123), 10 ms apart (atMs 0..590), so every repeat falls inside the 30 s cache TTL and the whole burst fits in one second. Starting revision: the released starter a4d88ab (references/good.mjs keeps the 30 s per-customer cache; references/broken.mjs is the guidance change that removes it). Each implementation's observe(requests) produces one observation (requests, upstreamCalls, responses, logs, requirements) that evaluate() judges; limits are read from observation.requirements, not hardcoded.

checks.condition: The observation is an object; requirements has positive numeric maxRequestsPerSecond and cacheTtlMs and a forbiddenLogFragments array of non-empty strings; requests, upstreamCalls, responses and logs are arrays; every request and upstream call has a non-empty string customerCode and finite numeric atMs; every log entry is a string. Otherwise the run fails, because the requirements cannot be judged on missing evidence.

Grouping upstreamCalls by customerCode and ordering each customer's call times, every gap between consecutive calls for the same customer is >= requirements.cacheTtlMs. A refresh exactly cacheTtlMs later is valid; calls for different customers never conflict.

For every upstream call at time t, the number of upstreamCalls with atMs in [t, t + 1000) is <= requirements.maxRequestsPerSecond. Counts calls that reached claims-core, not incoming requests; checking windows that start at each call covers every rolling one-second window.
No string in logs contains any entry of requirements.forbiddenLogFragments as a substring (case-sensitive). Other log text is allowed.
